rs-dr-safety.front: Why gloves and a stick for coyote, fox or wolf scat?
rs-dr-safety.back: They can carry Echinococcus multilocularis, a tapeworm dangerous to people. Rare, but easy to prevent. Wash with soap.
rs-dr-safety.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 322" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Scat safety: wear nitrile gloves every time, open droppings with a stick, do not sniff close to your face, and wash with soap before food. Coyote, fox and wolf scat can carry a dangerous tapeworm.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="322" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Safety first</text>
<rect x="16" y="62" width="180" height="88" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#dfe6d3" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="106" y="98" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Gloves</text><text x="106" y="124" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">nitrile, every time</text><rect x="204" y="62" width="180" height="88" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#dfe6d3" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="294" y="98" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Stick</text><text x="294" y="124" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">open it with a stick</text><rect x="16" y="162" width="180" height="88" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#dfe6d3" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="106" y="198" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">No sniffing</text><text x="106" y="224" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">not close to the face</text><rect x="204" y="162" width="180" height="88" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#dfe6d3" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="294" y="198" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Wash</text><text x="294" y="224" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">soap before food</text><rect x="16" y="268" width="368" height="44" rx="8" fill="#f6e3d8"/><text x="200" y="288" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#c62828" text-anchor="middle">Coyote, fox, wolf scat can carry</text><text x="200" y="305" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#c62828" text-anchor="middle">a dangerous tapeworm (85%)</text>
</svg>

rs-dr-bc-case.front: Where was BC's first known Echinococcus multilocularis case?
rs-dr-bc-case.back: A dog near Quesnel, 2009. Later found in coyotes and foxes there.

rs-dr-pile.front: Deer pellets in a pile beside a flattened oval?
rs-dr-pile.back: The deer bedded or stood here. Scattered pellets mean it was moving.

rs-dr-count.front: Can you count deer from pellet piles?
rs-dr-count.back: No. One deer drops about 13 to 34 pellet groups a day.

rs-dr-porcupine.front: Big piles of curved pellets at a den mouth or under a tree?
